questions.q: If the shortest distance between the straight lines $3 ( x - 1 ) = 6 ( y - 2 ) = 2 ( z - 1 )$ and $4 ( x - 2 ) = 2 ( y - \lambda ) = ( z - 3 ) , \lambda \in R$ is $\dfrac{1}{38},$~then the integral value of $\lambda$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The given lines are& $3 ( x - 1 ) = 6 ( y - 2 ) = 2 ( z - 1 )$~and~$4 ( x - 2 ) = 2 ( y - \lambda ) = ( z - 3 )$

And, they can be written as~${L}_{1}: \dfrac{( x - 1 )}{2} = \dfrac{( y - 2 )}{1} = \dfrac{( z - 1 )}{3}$~and~

${L}_{2}: \dfrac{( x - 2 )}{1} = \dfrac{y - \lambda}{2} = \dfrac{z - 3}{4} .$

The lines are in the form~$\dfrac{x - {x}_{1}}{l} = \dfrac{y - {y}_{1}}{m} = \dfrac{z - {z}_{1}}{n},$~where~ \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}, {z}_{1}\right)$~is a point on the line and~$l, m, n$~are the direction ratios of the vector parallel to the line.

Thus, the position vectors of the points on the line are respectively $\overset{→}{a1} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k} \text{ and } \overset{→}{a2} = 2\overset{^}{i} + \lambda\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$~and~direction of the lines are along the vectors~$\overset{→}{r}1 = 2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$~and~$\overset{→}{r2} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k} .$

Thus, we have~$\overset{→}{a} = \overset{→}{a2} - \overset{→}{a1} = \overset{^}{i} + \left(\lambda - 2\right)\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k} .$

Shortest distance =~Projection of $\overset{→}{a}$ on $\overset{→}{r1} \times \overset{→}{r2}$

$= \left|\overset{→}{a} \cdot \left(\overset{→}{r1} \times \overset{→}{r2}\right)\right|\left|\overset{→}{r1} \times \overset{→}{r2}\right|$

Now~$\overset{→}{r1} \times \overset{→}{r2} = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 4\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ \overset{→}{r1} \times \overset{→}{r2} = \overset{^}{i} \left(4 - 6\right) - \overset{^}{j} \left($8 - 3\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(4 - 1\right)$

$⇒ \overset{→}{r1} \times \overset{→}{r2} = -2\overset{^}{i} - 5\overset{^}{j} + 3\overset{^}{k}$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{r1} \times \overset{→}{r2}\right| = $\sqrt{\left(- 2\right)2 + \left(- 5\right)2 + {3}^{2}} = \sqrt{4 + 25 + 9} = \sqrt{38}

And,~\left|\overset{→}{a} \cdot \left(\overset{→}{r1} \times \overset{→}{r}2\right)\right| = \left|$\begin{cases}1 & \lambda - 2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 & 4\end{cases}\right|$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a} \cdot \left(\overset{→}{r1} \times \overset{→}{r}2\right)\right| = \left|1\left(4 - 6\right) - \left(\lambda -2\right)\left(8 - 3\right) + 2\left(4 - 1\right)\right|$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a} \cdot \left(\overset{→}{r1} \times \overset{→}{r}2\right)\right| = \left|-2 - 5\lambda + 10 + 6\right|$

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{a} \cdot \left(\overset{→}{r1} \times \overset{→}{r}2\right)\right| = \left|14 - 5\lambda\right|$

Given, the shortest distance is~\dfrac{1}{38},~hence, we have

\dfrac{1}{38} = \left|$14 - 5\lambda\right|$\sqrt{38}

$⇒ \left|14 - 5\lambda\right| = 1$

$⇒ 14 - 5\lambda = 1$~or $14 - 5\lambda = - 1$

$⇒ \lambda = $\dfrac{13}{5}~or~$3$

$∴$ Integral value is~$\lambda = 3 .$

Given lines are $\dfrac{x - 6}{1} = \dfrac{y - 4}{0} = \dfrac{z - 8}{3}$ and $\dfrac{x - 5}{2} = \dfrac{y - 1}{- 3} = \dfrac{z - 5}{6}$.

So, equation of $AB$ is,

\dfrac{x - 7}{2} = \dfrac{y + 2}{- 3} = \dfrac{z - 11}{6} = \lambda \left(\text{let}\right)$

$⇒ x = 2\lambda + 7, y = - 3\lambda - 2, z = 6\lambda + 11$

$⇒ B ≡ ( 2\lambda + 7, - 3\lambda - 2, 6\lambda + 11 )$

Also, the point $B$ lies on \dfrac{x - 6}{1} = \dfrac{y - 4}{0} = \dfrac{z - 8}{3}.

$⇒ $\dfrac{2\lambda + 7 - 6}{1} = \dfrac{- 3\lambda - 2 - 4}{0} = \dfrac{6\lambda + 11 - 8}{3}

$⇒ - 3\lambda - 2 - 4 = 0$

$⇒ - 3\lambda = 6$

$⇒ \lambda = - 2$

$⇒ B ≡ ( 3, 4, - 1 )$

$⇒ AB = $\sqrt{( 7 - 3{)}^{2} + ( 4 + 2{)}^{2} + ( 11 + 1{)}^{2}}

$⇒ AB = $\sqrt{16 + 36 + 144}

$⇒ AB = $\sqrt{196}

$⇒ AB = 14$

Lines& $\overset{→}{r} = \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right) ++l\left($2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$ and~$\overset{→}{r} = \left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right) + m\left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)$

Clearly both lines do not have same direction means lines are not parallel.

$⇒$Lines are skew lines or intersecting lines.

Let lines are skew lines and distance between lines is~$d$~if distance between them comes out zero then they will be intersecting lines.

For lines~$\overset{→}{r} = \overset{→}{a} + \lambda\overset{→}{p}, \overset{→}{r} = \overset{→}{b} + \lambda\overset{→}{q}$

$d = \left(\overset{→}{b} - \overset{→}{a}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{→}{p} \times \overset{→}{q}\right)\left|\overset{→}{p} \times \overset{→}{q}\right|$

Applying here

$d = \left(2\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right)\right) \cdot \left(\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \times \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)\right) \left|\left(2\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right)\times \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right)\right|$

$d = \left(\overset{^}{i}\right) \cdot \left(- \overset{^}{i} +3\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)\left|- \overset{^}{i} +3\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right| = \left|- $\dfrac{1}{14}\right| = \dfrac{1}{14}

$⇒$Lines are skew lines means do not intersect.

$

questions.q: The vertices $B$ and $C$ of a~$\Delta ABC$ lie on the line, $\dfrac{x + 2}{3} = \dfrac{y - 1}{0} = \dfrac{z}{4}$ such that $BC = 5$ units. Then the area (in sq. units) of this triangle, given the point $A\left(1, - 1, 2\right),$ is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The points& $B$~and~$C$~lie on the line~$\dfrac{x + 2}{3} = \dfrac{y - 1}{0} = \dfrac{z}{4} .$

Draw perpendicular~$AD$~on the line~$BC .$


Clearly area of~$\Delta ABC = \dfrac{1}{2} ⋅ AD ⋅ BC$

To find a point on the line, let~$\dfrac{x + 2}{3} = \dfrac{y - 1}{0} = \dfrac{z}{4} = r$

$⇒ x + 2 = 3r, y - 1 = 0, z = 4r$

$⇒ x = 3r - 2, y = 1, z = 4r$

Thus, the~point $D ≡ \left(3r - 2, 1, 4r\right)$

The direction ratios of a line joining two points~ \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}, {z}_{1}\right)$~and~ \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}, {z}_{2}\right)$are~

Thus, the direction ratios~of $AD$~are~=

Since $AD$ is perpendicular to given line, hence the dot product of their direction ratios is zero.

$⇒ 3 \cdot \left(3r - 3\right) + 0 \cdot2 + 4 \cdot \left(4r - 2\right) = 0$

$⇒ 9r - 9 + 16r - 8 = 0$

$⇒ 25r - 17 = 0$

$⇒ r = $\dfrac{17}{25}

$⇒ D ≡ \left(3 \times $\dfrac{17}{25} -$2, 1, 4 \times $\dfrac{17}{25}\right) = $\left(\dfrac{1}{25},$1, $\dfrac{68}{25})

The distance between the points~ \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}, {z}_{1}\right) & \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}, {z}_{2}\right)$~is~\sqrt{\left({x}_{1} - {x}_{2}\right)2 + \left({y}_{1} - {y}_{2}\right)2 + \left({z}_{1} - {z}_{2}\right)2}

$⇒ AD = $\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{1}{25} - 1\right)2 + \left(1 + 1\right)2 + \left(\dfrac{68}{25} - 2\right)2}

$⇒ AD = $\sqrt{\dfrac{576}{625} + 4 + \dfrac{324}{625}}

$⇒ AD = $\sqrt{\dfrac{136}{25}}

$⇒ AD = $\dfrac{2}{5}\sqrt{34}~units

Hence, the area of $\Delta ABC = $\dfrac{1}{2}$⋅ \left(\dfrac{2}{5}\sqrt{34})$⋅ 5 = $\sqrt{34} \text{ and } sq units.

$

questions.q: If the shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x + \sqrt{6}}{2} = \dfrac{y - \sqrt{6}}{3} = \dfrac{z - \sqrt{6}}{4}$~and~$\dfrac{x - \lambda}{3} = \dfrac{y - 2\sqrt{6}}{4} = \dfrac{z + 2\sqrt{6}}{5}$~is~$6$, then sum of squares of all possible values(s) of~$\lambda$& is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given equations are

$\dfrac{x - \lambda}{3} = \dfrac{y - 2\sqrt{6}}{4} = \dfrac{z + 2\sqrt{6}}{5}$~is passing through a point~ \left(\lambda, 2\sqrt{6}, 3\sqrt{6}\right)$~and it's direction ratios are~$3, 4, 5$.

So,~

$\overset{→}{a}1 = \lambda\overset{^}{i} + 2\sqrt{6}\overset{^}{j} - 2\sqrt{6}\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{b}1 = 3\overset{^}{i} + 4\overset{^}{j} + 5\overset{^}{k}$

And,

$\dfrac{x + \sqrt{6}}{2} = \dfrac{y - \sqrt{6}}{3} = \dfrac{z - \sqrt{6}}{4}$~is passing through a point~ \left(- \sqrt{6}, \sqrt{6}, \sqrt{6}\right)$~and it's direction ratios are~$1, 2, 3$.

$\overset{→}{a}2 = - \sqrt{6}\overset{^}{i} + \sqrt{6}\overset{^}{j} + \sqrt{6}\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{b}2 = 2\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k}$

Now,

$\overset{→}{a}2 - \overset{→}{a}1 = \left(- \sqrt{6}\overset{^}{i} + \sqrt{6}\overset{^}{j} + \sqrt{6}\overset{^}{k}\right) - \left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} + 2\sqrt{6}\overset{^}{j} - 2\sqrt{6}\overset{^}{k}\right) = - \left(\sqrt{6} + \lambda\right)\overset{^}{i} - \sqrt{6}\overset{^}{j} + 3\sqrt{6}\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2 = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 4\end{cases}$\right|$

$⇒ \overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2 = \left(\overset{^}{i} -2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)$

So,

$⇒ \left|\overset{→}{b}1 \times \overset{→}{b}2\right| = $\sqrt{6}

We know that the shortest distance between two skew lines is~ \left| \left(\overset{→}{a}$2 - \overset{→}{a}1\right)$\cdot \left(\overset{→}{b}$1 $\times \overset{→}{b}$2\right)\right|\left|\overset{→}{b}$1 $\times \overset{→}{b}$2\right| = 6$

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{\left(\left(- \sqrt{6} - \lambda\right)\overset{^}{i} - \sqrt{6}\overset{^}{j} + 3\sqrt{6}\overset{^}{k}\right) \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}\right)}{6}\right| =$6$

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{4\sqrt{6} - \lambda}{6}\right| =$6$

$⇒ \lambda = 10$\sqrt{6}, -$2$\sqrt{6}

So, required sum is

$= \left($10$\sqrt{6} -$2$\sqrt{6}\right)$2 = 384

$

questions.q: The distance of the point $P  \left(3, 4, 4\right)$ from the point of intersection of the line joining the points~$Q  \left(3, - 4, - 5\right)$ and $R  \left(2, - 3, 1\right)$ and the plane $2x + y + z = 7,& is equal to _____.$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have, point $P \left(3, 4, 4\right)$

Equation of~line joining the points~$Q \left(3, - 4, - 5\right)$ and $R \left(2, - 3, 1\right)$~is~\dfrac{x - 3}{- 1} = \dfrac{y + 4}{1} = \dfrac{z + 5}{6} =$r$

Any point on above line is~ \left(-$r + 3, r - 4, 6r - 5\right)$

Now, satisfying it in the given plane $2x + y + z = 7,$~we get

2\left(-$r + 3\right) + \left($r - 4\right) + \left($6r - 5\right) = 7$

$⇒ r = 2$

So, required point of intersection is T\left($1, - 2, 7\right) .$

Hence, $PT = \sqrt{\left(3 - 1\right)2 + \left(4 + 2\right)2 + \left(4 - 7\right)2} =7 .$
